summary: Brazil admits citizens of the EU, the UK and most of Latin America visa-free for up to 90 days, has required an eVisa (USD 80.90) from US, Canadian and Australian citizens since April 10, 2025, and asks the remaining nationalities to apply at a Brazilian consulate.

passportValidity.text: Brazil requires your passport to be valid for the duration of your stay. eVisa applicants need a passport valid for at least one month after arrival in Brazil, but check with your airline, which may expect more; at least 6 months' validity is recommended.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: Not an entry requirement: Brazil's Ministry of Health says no proof of vaccination is required to enter the country. Vaccination is recommended at least 10 days before travel to areas where it is advised, including the Amazon, the Pantanal, Iguaçu Falls and most inland states, and several onward countries require proof of vaccination from travelers who have been in Brazil.

source.name: Ministério da Saúde — Vaccination for travellers

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel insurance requirement for Brazil.

onwardTicket.text: Customs officials may ask to see a return or onward ticket, according to Canada's travel advice. No Brazilian government page we could read states the rule.

source.name: Government of Canada — Travel advice: Brazil (entry and exit requirements)

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is set, but officials may ask for proof of sufficient funds to cover your stay, according to Canada's travel advice. Consular visa applicants must document their income.

source.name: Government of Canada — Travel advice: Brazil (entry and exit requirements)

currencyLimits.text: Cash of more than USD 10,000 (or the equivalent in any other currency) must be declared electronically (e-DBV) to customs on entry, and a declaration also applies on departure.

source.name: Receita Federal — Traveller's Guide: cash on entry to Brazil

notes: According to the Receita Federal, goods that are not for personal use are duty-free up to US$1,000 when you arrive by air or sea, or US$500 by other routes, with a separate US$1,000 allowance for the arrival duty-free shop at your first Brazilian airport.

payments.text: According to the Government of Canada, credit and debit cards are widely accepted in cities, restaurants and stores but less so in rural or informal markets, ATMs are scarce in rural areas, and you should carry cash for small transactions and remote areas.

safety.text: Violent and street crime are real risks in Brazilian cities: keep phones and jewellery out of sight, use app taxis at night, avoid deserted areas and beaches after dark, and avoid favelas altogether, including favela tours marketed to tourists.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Brazil travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: No official seasonal guidance. The Government of Canada gives the rainy seasons as January to July in the north, October to April in the south and southeast, and April to July in the northeast, and says Brasília and the interior have extreme dry periods from May to October.

idp.text: Brazil is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

driving.text: Brazil is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Brazil yet.

The UK FCDO says robberies are common in many cities and that thieves target mobile phones, particularly between 4pm and 9pm. It advises against using a phone in the street, hailing taxis on the street, or resisting an attacker.
Brazil has more than one mains voltage: the IEC lists both 127 V and 220 V. Check the outlet label before plugging in.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Brazil?
faq.answer: Yes. Since April 10, 2025, US citizens need an eVisa to visit Brazil. It costs USD 80.90, is applied for online at brazil.vfsevisa.com, and for US citizens is issued with up to 10 years' validity, allowing stays of up to 90 days per visit and 180 days per year.

faq.question: Which nationalities can visit Brazil without a visa?
faq.answer: Citizens of the EU, the UK, Switzerland, Japan, South Korea, Turkey, South Africa, Mexico and most of South America (among others) can visit visa-free for up to 90 days. US, Canadian and Australian citizens need the eVisa, and nationalities such as Indian and Nigerian citizens need a consular visa.

faq.question: How do I apply for the Brazilian eVisa?
faq.answer: Apply online at the official portal brazil.vfsevisa.com with a colour copy of your passport bio page and a recent photograph, and pay USD 80.90. The portal says processing takes up to 10 business days once your verified application is submitted, so apply well before travel.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Brazil?
faq.answer: No, it is not an entry requirement: Brazil's Ministry of Health says no proof of vaccination is required to enter the country. Vaccination is recommended at least 10 days before travel to areas where it is advised, including the Amazon, the Pantanal, Iguaçu Falls and most inland states, and some countries you travel to afterward will demand the certificate because you have been in Brazil.

faq.question: Can I extend my 90-day stay in Brazil?
faq.answer: Most visa-free and eVisa visitors can apply to the Federal Police (Polícia Federal) before their first 90 days expire for one extension of up to 90 days, within an overall cap of 180 days in any 12-month period. Some nationalities (for example Germans and Italians) are capped at 90 days per 180-day period.
